pairs.subject: accessibility
pairs.evidence: packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/rules/enforce-reduced-motion-fallback.cjs:152 The reduced-motion lint rule exits on non-repeating animations and permits arbitrary non-essential entrance and slide motion without fallbacks, deviating from the preference-respect contract.

techniques.evidence: packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/rules/enforce-reduced-motion-fallback.cjs:152 The rule checks only looping animations and skips non-repeating transitions, allowing non-essential entrance and slide motion without reduced-motion fallbacks.

packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/rules/role-button-requires-keydown.cjs:53 The check passes non-button elements with role='button' and onClick if onKeyDown is present, without requiring tabIndex to ensure keyboard focusability in the tab order.

packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/rules/role-button-requires-keydown.cjs:43 The rule legitimizes custom non-button containers with role='button' as long as keydown is handled, rather than enforcing native button elements or shared primitives that encapsulate the full contract.

packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/rules/enforce-reduced-motion-fallback.cjs:159 The lint check observes a proxy by exempting animations whenever a fallback identifier token exists anywhere in the enclosing scope, without verifying that motion is actually gated.
packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/package.json:5 The context is an ESLint rule plugin rather than a UI component managing hidden-but-mounted subtrees or DOM inertness.
packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/index.cjs:2 The context provides static AST lint rules and does not mount an application shell or live region announcement provider.

packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/package.json:32 The package specifies an ESLint engine peer dependency and does not define a held assistive technology pairing list or screen reader workarounds.

pairs.registryProposal: Consider clarifying in preference-respect and a11y-verification whether static AST linting rules are recognized as a static enforcement gate or if static linters that observe identifier proxies rather than rendered/runtime behavior constitute verification gaps.
